**Nedim Bajrami** (born 28 February 1999) is a footballer who plays as an [attacking midfielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attacking_midfielder "Attacking midfielder") or [winger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winger_\(association_football\) "Winger \(association football\)") for [Saudi Pro League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Pro_League "Saudi Pro League") club [Al Taawoun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Taawoun_FC "Al Taawoun FC"), on loan from [Scottish Premiership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Premiership "Scottish Premiership") club [Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rangers_F.C. "Rangers F.C."). Born in Switzerland, he plays for the [Albania national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albania_national_football_team "Albania national football team").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-Soccerway-1)
Bajrami began his professional career at [Grasshopper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grasshopper_Club_Zurich "Grasshopper Club Zurich") in Switzerland before moving to [Empoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empoli_F.C. "Empoli F.C.") in 2019 to help the club gain promotion to Serie A in 2021. He then joined [Sassuolo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Sassuolo_Calcio "U.S. Sassuolo Calcio") in 2023, and moved to [Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rangers_F.C. "Rangers F.C.") in Scotland in 2024.
Internationally, he represented Switzerland at youth levels before switching allegiance to [Albania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albania_national_football_team "Albania national football team") in 2021. In June 2024, Bajrami represented Albania at [UEFA Euro 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2024 "UEFA Euro 2024") and scored the fastest goal in [tournament history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship_records_and_statistics "UEFA European Championship records and statistics"), after just 23 seconds.
## Club career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nedim_Bajrami&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Club career")]
### Early career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nedim_Bajrami&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early career")]
Born in Switzerland to [Albanian parents from Macedonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albanians_in_North_Macedonia "Albanians in North Macedonia"), with his father from [Tetovo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetovo "Tetovo") and his mother from [Gostivar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gostivar "Gostivar").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-4) He is the third generation of his family in Switzerland. Bajrami grew up in [Regensdorf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Regensdorf?action=edit&redlink=1 "FC Regensdorf \(page does not exist\)") and started playing football at age six with the local club. He was later scouted by [Grasshoppers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grasshopper_Club_Z%C3%BCrich "Grasshopper Club Zürich") and joined their youth system from the U-8 level, progressing through all academy categories. He won the Swiss qualifying round of the Nike Cup with the U-15 team and the Swiss Cup at U-16 level.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-5)
### Grasshoppers
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nedim_Bajrami&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Grasshoppers")]
In February 2017, he signed his first professional contract with the [Grasshoppers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grasshopper_Club_Z%C3%BCrich "Grasshopper Club Zürich") senior team, alongside [Petar Pušić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petar_Pu%C5%A1i%C4%87 "Petar Pušić") and [Arijan Qollaku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijan_Qollaku "Arijan Qollaku").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-6) He made his professional debut on 5 February 2017 in the [Swiss Super League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swiss_Super_League "Swiss Super League"), playing the full 90 minutes in a 1–0 defeat against [FC Thun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Thun "FC Thun").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-7)
#### Breakthrough and establishment (2017–2019)
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nedim_Bajrami&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Breakthrough and establishment \(2017–2019\)")]
In the 2017–18 season, at 18 years old, Bajrami became a regular starter in Grasshoppers’ midfield, making 32 league appearances and scoring 3 goals.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-Soccerway-1) He scored a decisive goal in the 2–1 victory over [Zürich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Z%C3%BCrich "FC Zürich") on 21 October 2017.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-8)
In the 2018–19 season, Bajrami made 33 league appearances and scored 3 goals.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-9)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-Soccerway-1) He became a central figure in midfield and attracted attention from scouts abroad.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-10)
By the end of 2018–19, Bajrami had around 80 competitive appearances for Grasshoppers, scoring 6 goals, establishing himself as a key player before his move to Empoli.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-Soccerway-1)
### Empoli
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nedim_Bajrami&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Empoli")]
On 13 August 2019, Bajrami joined [Serie B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_B "Serie B") club [Empoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empoli_F.C. "Empoli F.C.") on loan with an option to buy.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-11) During the 2019–20 season, he became a regular starter, making over 30 appearances and scoring five goals.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-Soccerway-1) In July 2020, Empoli exercised the purchase option and signed him on a permanent deal.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-12)
In the [2020–21 Serie B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020%E2%80%9321_Serie_B "2020–21 Serie B") season, he scored five goals and provided eight assists as Empoli won the league and secured promotion to [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-13) On 4 May 2021, he scored in a 4–0 victory against Cosenza, confirming the club's promotion.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-15)
#### 2021–23: Serie A period, Coppa Italia, goals, assists and departure
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nedim_Bajrami&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2021–23: Serie A period, Coppa Italia, goals, assists and departure")]
On 15 August 2021, Bajrami scored the opening goal in the [2021–22 Coppa Italia first round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Coppa_Italia#First_round "2021–22 Coppa Italia") against [Vicenza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vicenza_Calcio "Vicenza Calcio") in the 10th minute, with the match finishing as a 4–2 victory.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-17) On 21 August 2021, he made his Serie A debut in a 3–1 loss against [Lazio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Lazio "SS Lazio").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-18) On 11 September 2021, Bajrami scored his first Serie A goal from the penalty spot in a 2–1 loss against [Venezia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezia_FC "Venezia FC").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-19) On 26 September 2021, he scored from the penalty spot in a 4–2 win against [Bologna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bologna_F.C._1909 "Bologna F.C. 1909"), marking Empoli's third victory in their opening six league matches.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-21) On 6 December 2021, he scored and assisted in a 3–1 win against [Udinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udinese_Calcio "Udinese Calcio"), helping the club to a comeback and a third consecutive unbeaten league match at the time.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-23) On 22 December 2021, Bajrami scored once in matchday 19 fixture against [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan"), finding the net in the 18th minute despite Empoli eventually being defeated 4–2. [[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-24) In the Coppa Italia, Bajrami also scored in the second round and in the Round of 16 in December and January respectively, where Empoli were narrowly eliminated 3–2 by [Inter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-25) On 6 January 2022, Bajrami scored a penalty in a 3–3 draw against Lazio.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-27) On 23 January 2022, he scored his sixth Serie A goal in a 2–4 loss against [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Roma "AS Roma").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-28) On 13 February 2022, Bajrami provided an assist in a 1–1 draw away to [Cagliari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cagliari_Calcio "Cagliari Calcio").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-29) On 21 May 2022, he assisted [Leo Štulac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leo_%C5%A0tulac "Leo Štulac")’s 79th‑minute goal in a 1–0 away win over [Atalanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atalanta_BC "Atalanta BC").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-31) On 24 April 2022, he assisted Andrea Pinamonti for Empoli's third goal in a 3–2 win against [Napoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SSC_Napoli "SSC Napoli").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-33) During the 2021–22 Serie A season, he made 35 appearances, including 23 as a starter, scoring six goals and providing five assists.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-35)
On 1 October 2022, Bajrami scored in a [2022–23 Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A "2022–23 Serie A") round 8 match against Milan, with Empoli losing 3–1.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-36) On 23 January 2023, he assisted the only goal in a 1–0 win away to Inter Milan in Round 19.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-37) In the first half of the 2022–23 season, he made 18 Serie A appearances, scoring one goal and providing one assist.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-38)
Overall, Bajrami made more than 120 competitive appearances for Empoli, scoring 18 goals and providing over 20 assists.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-39)
### Sassuolo
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nedim_Bajrami&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Sassuolo")]
On 31 January 2023, Bajrami joined [Sassuolo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Sassuolo_Calcio "U.S. Sassuolo Calcio") in [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A") on loan, with an obligation to buy reportedly set at around €7 million.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-41) He made his debut a week later against [Cremonese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Cremonese "US Cremonese"), scoring the winning goal in stoppage time in a 3–2 victory.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-43) During the remainder of the [2022–23 Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A "2022–23 Serie A") season, he made 23 league appearances and provided two assists.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-Soccerway-1) The transfer was made permanent at the end of the season following the mandatory purchase clause.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-44)
In the [2023–24 Coppa Italia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_Coppa_Italia "2023–24 Coppa Italia"), Bajrami scored one goal in the first round, and Sassuolo were eventually eliminated in the Round of 16 after a 3–1 loss to [Atalanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atalanta_BC "Atalanta BC").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-45) On 27 September 2023, Bajrami scored his first league goal of the season in his sixth league appearance, netting in a 2–1 away win against [Inter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan") on matchday six of the [2023–24 Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_Serie_A "2023–24 Serie A"), after which head coach [Alessio Dionisi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alessio_Dionisi "Alessio Dionisi") praised his performance.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-46) In April 2024, he scored a goal and provided an assist within seven minutes in the first half of a league match against Salernitana.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-47) Italian media described him as an attacking midfielder and highlighted his creativity, impact in decisive moments and ability to provide key passes.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-48) In total, he made 28 league appearances, scoring two goals and providing multiple assists.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-Soccerway-1)
Following Sassuolo's relegation to Serie B at the end of the 2023–24 season, transfer speculation surrounded Bajrami. Reports in August 2024 linked him with a move to Scottish club Rangers for a reported fee of around €4 million.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-49) However, Italian outlets also reported that Sassuolo were considering keeping him to play a role in their bid to return to Serie A.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-50)

"Rangers F.C.") in the [Scottish Premiership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Premiership "Scottish Premiership").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-51) On 15 September 2024, Bajrami made his debut for Rangers in the league against [Dundee United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dundee_United_F.C. "Dundee United F.C."), coming on as a half-time substitute in a 1–0 away win.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-52) A week later, he made his first start for Rangers in a 3–0 win over Dundee in the [Scottish League Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_Scottish_League_Cup "2024–25 Scottish League Cup") quarter-final, providing the assist for Rangers’ third goal.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-53) He scored his first goal for the club on his [UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League "UEFA Europa League") debut on 26 September 2024, netting less than a minute into a 2–0 away win against [Malmö FF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malm%C3%B6_Fotbollf%C3%B6rening "Malmö Fotbollförening") in the [league phase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_UEFA_Europa_League_league_phase "2024–25 UEFA Europa League league phase").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-55) On 30 October 2024, he scored his first league goal for Rangers in his sixth appearance in the competition, striking a diagonal left-footed shot in the 63rd minute to equalise in a 1–1 draw against [Aberdeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aberdeen_F.C. "Aberdeen F.C.").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-56) Four days later, he scored the winning goal in the semi-final of the [Scottish League Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_Scottish_League_Cup "2024–25 Scottish League Cup"), as Rangers defeated [Motherwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motherwell_F.C. "Motherwell F.C.") 2–1 at Hampden Park to reach the final.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-58) On 15 December 2024, in the [League Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Scottish_League_Cup_final "2024 Scottish League Cup final"), Bajrami opened the scoring for Rangers in a 3–3 draw against Celtic at Hampden Park, before Rangers were defeated 5–4 in the ensuing penalty shoot-out.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-60)
By the end of the 2024–25 season, Bajrami had made 47 appearances in all competitions for Rangers, scoring five goals and providing five assists.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-62)

"Alloa Athletic F.C.").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-67) Thereafter, in domestic competitions Bajrami continued to be used sparingly during September and October, featuring only as a late substitute.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-Soccerway-1) After starting for the [Albania national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albania_national_football_team "Albania national football team") in November 2025 in their final [2026 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group K](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_%E2%80%93_UEFA_Group_K "2026 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group K") match against the [England national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England_national_football_team "England national football team"), Bajrami was given minutes in Rangers’ next league fixture, after having not featured for the club for a month and a half.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-68)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-Soccerway-1)
On 24 November 2025, Rangers dismissed sporting director [Kevin Thelwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Thelwell "Kevin Thelwell") and chief executive Patrick Stewart following the short tenure of former manager [Russell Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell_Martin_\(footballer\) "Russell Martin \(footballer\)"), with reports indicating that Bajrami had not been considered for selection for an extended period under the previous management structure, before returning to receive playing time after the appointment of head coach [Danny Röhl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_R%C3%B6hl "Danny Röhl"), who subsequently made positive comments about him.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-69) A week later, Bajrami made his first league start of the season, playing 75 minutes against [Falkirk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falkirk_F.C. "Falkirk F.C."), and was subsequently named in the Team of the Week.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-70) Four days later, Bajrami scored his first goal of the season, converting a penalty in the 90+8th minute to secure a 2–2 draw against Dundee United.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-71) On 27 January 2026, Bajrami returned to action for Rangers after recovering from a muscle injury sustained on 6 December 2025 against [Kilmarnock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilmarnock_F.C. "Kilmarnock F.C."), when he was forced to leave the field after around 21 minutes, though the club reportedly considered a potential transfer due to limited playing opportunities this season.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-72) On 22 February 2026, Bajrami came on as a 79th-minute substitute in Rangers' 2–2 away draw against [Livingston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Livingston_F.C. "Livingston F.C."), providing an assist two minutes later for [Emmanuel Fernández](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmanuel_Fernandez_\(footballer\) "Emmanuel Fernandez \(footballer\)")'s goal as his side recovered from a 2–0 deficit to equalise.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-73)

## International career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nedim_Bajrami&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: International career")]
### Switzerland
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nedim_Bajrami&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Switzerland")]
> "We tried to convince Bajrami to continue playing for Switzerland but he told us that his heart beats for Albania. For us in the national team, identification is one of the main values, so we had no choice but to let him leave."
— Mauro's explanation for Bajrami’s switch to Albania.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-75)
Bajrami represented Switzerland at various youth levels up to the [under-21](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland_national_under-21_football_team "Switzerland national under-21 football team") side. He featured for the [Switzerland U17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland_national_under-17_football_team "Switzerland national under-17 football team") team during the [2016 European Under-17 Championship qualification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_UEFA_European_Under-17_Championship_qualification "2016 UEFA European Under-17 Championship qualification") campaign, playing in all six matches.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-76) He scored five goals for the U17s, including a brace against [Montenegro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montenegro_national_under-17_football_team "Montenegro national under-17 football team") in August 2015.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-77) On 9 March 2021, Switzerland U21 manager [Mauro Lustrinelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauro_Lustrinelli "Mauro Lustrinelli") confirmed that Bajrami had chosen to switch allegiances to represent his country of [origin Albania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Origin_of_the_Albanians "Origin of the Albanians"), and expects invitation from [Albanian Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albanian_Football_Association "Albanian Football Association").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-78)
### Albania
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nedim_Bajrami&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Albania")]
On 17 March 2021, he obtained [Albanian citizenship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albanian_nationality_law "Albanian nationality law"), thus requiring only approval from [FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA "FIFA") to become eligible for the [Albania national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albania_national_football_team "Albania national football team").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-79) FIFA rejected the request, but he was subsequently cleared to play following a decision by the [Court of Arbitration for Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court_of_Arbitration_for_Sport "Court of Arbitration for Sport") on 30 August 2021.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-80) He debuted with Albania in a 1–0 [2022 FIFA World Cup qualification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_%E2%80%93_UEFA_Group_I "2022 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group I") victory against [Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary_national_football_team "Hungary national football team") on 5 September 2021, coming on as a substitute in the 63rd minute for [Qazim Laçi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qazim_La%C3%A7i "Qazim Laçi").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-81)
Following his transfer to Sassuolo in Winter 2023, Bajrami emerged as a key goalscoring contributor for Albania, netting three consecutive goals in the [UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2024_qualifying_Group_E "UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying Group E") campaign and adding two more later in the qualifiers, totaling five goals during the campaign.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-EU-Football-82) His first goal came on 17 June 2023 in a 2–0 win over [Moldova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldova_national_football_team "Moldova national football team").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-83) He appeared in all eight qualifying matches, recording three goals and one assist, as Albania for the first time in its history finished top of the group after collecting 15 points—level with the [Czech Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_Republic_national_football_team "Czech Republic national football team") but ahead on head-to-head record—and qualified for the final tournament of the [UEFA European Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship "UEFA European Championship") for the second time in its history.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-84)
In June 2024, Bajrami was selected for the Albanian squad at [UEFA Euro 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2024 "UEFA Euro 2024").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-85) In Albania's opening match against defending champions [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy_national_football_team "Italy national football team"), he scored after 23 seconds, setting the record for the fastest goal in [European Championship history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship_records_and_statistics "UEFA European Championship records and statistics"), though Albania eventually lost 2–1.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-86) In the second match, he played the full 90 minutes in a 2–2 draw against [Croatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_national_football_team "Croatia national football team"), in which Albania had initially taken the lead, and he also started in the final group match against [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_national_football_team "Spain national football team"), which Albania lost 1–0, resulting in their elimination from the tournament.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-87)
On 19 November 2024, he scored from the penalty spot against [Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine_national_football_team "Ukraine national football team") in the [2024–25 UEFA Nations League B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_UEFA_Nations_League_B "2024–25 UEFA Nations League B"), a match Albania lost 2–1, resulting in relegation to League C.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-88) During the [2026 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_\(UEFA\) "2026 FIFA World Cup qualification \(UEFA\)") campaign, Bajrami made six appearances for Albania in [Group K](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_%E2%80%93_UEFA_Group_K "2026 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group K"), including three starts, in matches where the team recorded three wins and one draw without conceding a goal, and finished second in the group with 14 points to secure qualification to the [play-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_%E2%80%93_UEFA_second_round "2026 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA second round") for the first time in its history.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-90) In the play-off on 26 March 2026 against [Poland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poland_national_football_team "Poland national football team"), Bajrami started in attack and played 67 minutes; in the 54th minute, he missed a clear chance from close range following a counterattack, as Albania lost 2–1 after initially taking the lead and was eliminated.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedim_Bajrami#cite_note-91)
